questions.prompt: What do we call the son of my sister?
steps: A sister's child is a niece or nephew.
A male child is a nephew.

questions.prompt: Choose the synonym of dislike.
steps: A synonym has a similar meaning and should fit the same grammatical role.
Hate is a verb expressing a stronger dislike.

questions.prompt: Which word means sad?
steps: Sad describes someone who does not feel happy.
Unhappy matches that meaning.

questions.prompt: My uncle attends and takes care of the sick in hospital. What is his occupation?
steps: The description focuses on nursing care of patients.
In this question, the intended occupation is nurse.
questions.tip: This is the answer identified in NECTA's examiner report. Several medical professions care for patients, so read the specific role described.

questions.prompt: Complete: The crops were attacked by a __ of locusts.
steps: The blank needs the collective noun for locusts.
A large group of these insects is a swarm.

questions.prompt: Do you __ any help? Choose need, needed or needing.
steps: The auxiliary do is followed by the base form of the main verb.
Use need without an ending.
questions.answer: Need: Do you need any help?

questions.prompt: I __ to the market last Saturday. Choose go, gone or went.
steps: Last Saturday indicates a completed past action.
The simple past of go is went.
questions.answer: Went: I went to the market last Saturday.

questions.prompt: Jumanne and Bakari are __ my sons. Choose all, both or either.
steps: The sentence names exactly two people.
Both includes the two together; either refers to one of them.
questions.answer: Both: Jumanne and Bakari are both my sons.

questions.prompt: May I __ the window? Choose close, closing or closed.
steps: The modal verb may is followed by the base form.
Choose close.
questions.answer: Close: May I close the window?

questions.prompt: It is very __ to drive too fast. Choose danger, dangerous or dangerously.
steps: The blank describes driving too fast after it is very.
Use an adjective, rather than a noun or adverb.
questions.answer: Dangerous: It is very dangerous to drive too fast.

questions.prompt: Assign the order letter to (i): I brush my teeth and take a bath.
steps: Introduce Florian first, then describe waking up.
Brushing and bathing follow waking, making this the third sentence.

questions.prompt: Assign the order letter to (ii): After taking a bath, I eat my breakfast.
steps: The phrase after taking a bath places this after sentence (i).
Breakfast is the fourth event in the completed sequence.

questions.prompt: Confirm the given example (iii): My name is Florian.
steps: A self-introduction opens the account.
It is the first sentence.

questions.prompt: Assign the order letter to (iv): Thereafter, I put on my school uniform.
steps: Dressing follows breakfast and precedes leaving for school.
It is the fifth sentence.
questions.tip: The library's retyped paper says put on my breakfast. NECTA's examiner report gives school uniform; the order remains E.

questions.prompt: Assign the order letter to (v): I wake up early in the morning.
steps: Waking begins the day's actions after the introduction.
It precedes bathing and breakfast.

questions.prompt: Assign the order letter to (vi): Then I take my bag and leave for school.
steps: Leaving happens after waking, washing, breakfast and dressing.
This is the sixth and final sentence.

questions.prompt: What is the passage about?
steps: Identify the subject repeated throughout the passage.
It describes wild animals, their features and their behaviour.
questions.answer: The passage is about wild animals and their behaviour.

questions.prompt: Which animal has beautiful black spots?
steps: Locate the animal described with spots.
The passage assigns this feature to the cheetah.
questions.answer: The cheetah has beautiful black spots.

questions.prompt: How does a giraffe eat leaves on tall trees?
steps: Find the body part named in the giraffe's description.
Its long neck helps it reach the leaves.
questions.answer: A giraffe uses its long neck to reach and eat leaves on tall trees.

questions.prompt: Why does the lion kill other animals?
steps: The printed question omits lion, but the passage identifies the animal.
The passage gives obtaining food as the reason.
questions.answer: The lion kills other animals for food.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the behaviour of the zebra and the giraffe?
steps: In the passage, these animals are described as kind.
Turn that description into a lesson about our behaviour.
questions.answer: We should be kind and gentle towards others.
questions.tip: Answer according to the passage. Observe wild animals safely; the story's description is not advice to touch them.

summaries.Section A: Dictation: Practise listening, word spacing, capital letters and punctuation. Ask someone to read each sentence aloud before you check it.
summaries.Section B: Vocabulary: Read the complete sentence. Check the exact meaning, relationship, occupation or collective noun before choosing its letter.
summaries.Section C: Grammar: Check the subject, time expression, noun type and any auxiliary verb before selecting the correct grammatical form.
summaries.Section D: Composition: Use context and grammar together. Read the whole composition again to check that the completed ideas connect logically.
summaries.Section E: Comprehension: Locate evidence in the passage, then answer in your own clear sentence. Support a moral or lesson with what happened in the story.
